did: I built the workflow that deletes the branches a merged bucket carried, since cloud sessions can't delete branches themselves. It rode in bucket 3. After three fresh reviews and a fix for merge-commit merges, it ran for buckets 1, 2 and 3 and deleted the eleven worker branches they carried, keeping the ones that had moved on. Its first real run found one more bug: my own worker branch, claude/bucket-prune, was kept because its name starts like a bucket's. I fixed that in its own defect PR, #3413, so a bucket is now known only by its exact name, then re-ran the prune and that branch is gone.

calls.title: Which branches a bucket prune deletes
options: Only branches whose tip is a commit a bucket merge brought in
Every branch whose tip is off main and inside the bucket's head
calls.why: The first missed a branch the bucket was started from. Every tip inside the head has all its work on main, so the wider rule loses nothing, and the keep rules still guard bots, buckets, protected branches and open pull requests.
calls.undo: Narrow the delete condition in scripts/bucket-prune.sh back to tips equal to a merged parent.

calls.title: Measuring a bucket from main as it was just before the merge
options: The first parent of the PR's merge commit
calls.why: Bucket 2 merged with a merge commit, after which main holds the whole bucket and nothing reads as carried. The merge commit's parent works for a squash, a merge commit and a rebase alike.
calls.undo: Change the plan call in run to measure against the default branch's tip.

calls.title: A merged PR whose branch only looks like a bucket's
options: Pass with a notice and prune nothing
calls.why: The workflow's filter can only test the name's start, so an ordinary merge from such a branch would otherwise turn red for nothing. A manual dispatch for one is still refused.
calls.undo: In run, drop the early exit for pull_request events so the head check fails instead.

left: Branches protected only by a ruleset aren't read from the API. Deleting one is refused and the run goes red naming it, which fails safe.
The server's copy is server#1107, filed by the coordinator, because this session couldn't write to paulgsc/server; it should match bucket names the way #3413 does.
